name: 2S19 Msta-S

placement_rationale.text: 2S19 Msta-S's real-world range (per this asset's own Wikipedia source) runs about 24.7 km with standard rounds up to ~36 km with rocket-assisted projectiles, so 18 km uses roughly half to three-quarters of that envelope depending on round type — a narrower margin than the NATO-donated SPGs in this comparison set, though still short of firing at true max range. Russian artillery employment has historically favored denser, closer massed fires rather than the wide dispersion-and-displacement discipline doctrine.md §2 documents becoming standard elsewhere on this battlefield, so a tighter standoff than its Ukrainian-side counterparts is plausible for this platform rather than an error. 18 km still sits inside doctrine.md's 10–150+ km medium/long-range strike band, outside the close 0–10 km FPV strike zone.

Strength: Well-proven, mass-produced Russian standard SPG with a large existing fleet and logistics base
Limitation: Older-generation autoloader and fire-control compared to Western systems like PzH2000
Estimated quantity available: Large pre-war fleet; current operational count reduced by attrition, not fully disclosed
employment_notes: Russia's baseline standard SPG throughout the war, functionally the Russian-side counterpart to Ukraine's donated M109/PzH2000 in the tool's artillery comparison
contrast_vs_traditional: The same shoot-and-scoot pressure applies on the Russian side of the line: a tracked Soviet-lineage gun built for sustained fire missions now displaces as fast as its crew can manage once a round is downrange, because the drone spotting a firing position feeds counter-battery fire on the same minutes-scale timeline doctrine.md documents for the kill chain generally, not just for Ukrainian-fired systems.
